title: Isolation of single cells from individual mouse ovaries for flow cytometry and functional analysis
protocol: Collect vaginal lavage for cycle stage determination on the day of experiment.
Pipette 200 μL of sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and flush the mouse vagina three times.
Place the collected lavage in a labeled vial.
Mount cells on slides: Place 50-100 μL of vaginal lavage from each mouse on clean labeled microscope slides.
Allow the mounted cells to air-dry at room temperature.
Fix the dried slides with cold 100% methanol and allow them to air-dry.
Stain the fixed slides with 0.01% methylene blue for one minute.
Place the stained slides up to three at a time into the staining solution.
Remove slides from the methylene blue solution.
Place slides in a Coplin jar containing up to ¾ distilled or deionized water for 0.5–1 min.
Remove slides from water and place on a clean dry surface.
Wipe off excess water from the edges of the slides using Kimwipes.
Air-dry the slides and view under a microscope.
Process ovaries while the cells air-dry.
Withdraw up to 200 μL of lavage in case of spillage or loss due to handling.
Focus on an area of the slide that best represents the cell distribution at ×20 magnification.
Determine proestrus stage by identifying the dominant presence of nucleated epithelial cells punctuated with cornified epithelial and leukocytic cells.
Identify estrus stage by noting the dominant presence of anucleated cornified epithelial cells.
Identify metestrus stage by observing a fairly even mixed combination of leukocytic cells, nucleated epithelial cells, and cornified epithelial cells.
Determine diestrus stage by observing the dominant presence of leukocytic cells in vaginal smears.
Anesthetize the mouse under isoflurane anesthesia.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Spray 70% ethanol on the abdominal region.
Open the abdomen carefully with fine scissors to expose the abdominal cavity.
Identify the spleen located under the ribcage and harvest it.
Remove the intestines and abdominal fat from the abdominal cavity.
Locate the ovary which sits on top of the oviduct and uterus.
Harvest the mouse ovary.
Harvest the spleen and place it immediately in cold medium (RPMI + 20% FBS).
Gently push aside the intestines with forceps to reveal the reproductive tract underneath.
Identify the ovary and carefully dissect it from both uterine horns.
Place the isolated ovary immediately in a Petri dish containing cold media (RPMI + 20% FBS).
Rapidly but gently remove adhering fat and mesenteries if present.
Lightly place the ovaries on an adsorbent pad to remove excess fluid, then remove from the pad.
Weigh the cleaned ovaries.
Handle the ovary with care.
Weigh the ovaries for normalization relative to ovary weight.
Place mouse spleen in one pouch of the filtra blender bag.
Add approximately 3 mL phenol red RPMI media to the spleen.
Gently but thoroughly mash the spleen using the cap-end of a sample collection tube or syringe plunger.
Add 10 mL of PBS to the mashed spleen.
Aspirate the spleen cells from another pouch and place in a labeled 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 5 minutes at 4°C, then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 5 mL ACK Lysing Buffer and incubate at room temperature (20°C–26°C) for 5 minutes.
Add 20 mL of PBS to stop the ACK reaction, centrifuge again at 1200 rpm for 5 minutes at 4°C, then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 10 mL of FACS buffer.
Filter the suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or white blood cell counter and keep on ice.
Pre-fill labeled gentleMACS C tubes with digest solution containing 4.5 mL of RPMI and 0.1% collagenase IV at 0.5 mL.
Place 100 μL of digest solution on a Petri dish.
Lightly grip the ovary and mince it into small bits using sterile scissors.
Transfer minced ovaries back into the designated gentleMACS C tube using a serological pipet.
Secure the lid tightly on the tube (use Parafilm to seal if necessary).
Invert and insert the tubes with minced ovaries onto the dissociator holders.
Dissociate tissues using the custom program set at 20 minutes, temperature on (37°C), and repetition rate 400.
Remove tubes from the dissociator after the end of the program, revert to upright position.
Place tubes immediately on ice for 1 minute to begin quenching the reaction.
Pour cold tissue mix into a filtration or blender bag.
Gently mash remaining tissue pieces using the cap-end of the tube or syringe plunger.
Add 5 mL of phenol-red free RPMI media to further quench the reaction.
Label 50 mL tubes and place 40 μm strainers on each tube (keep tubes on ice).
Pipette out the fluid from the other side of the filtra blender bag and place immediately onto the strainer on the 50 mL tube.
Spin down at 1200 rpm for 5 min at 4°C.
Count cells using a hemocytometer for total cells or a White blood cell (WBC) counter for leukocyte counts.
Label 5 mL FACS tubes for each sample: compensation beads, single-stained cells, fluorescence-minus one stained cells (FMOs), fully stained samples, unstained samples.
Transfer cell suspensions into FACS tubes (∼0.5–1 million cells for unstained, single-stained and FMOs, and 2–5 million cells for fully stained samples).
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 100 μL Zombie Aqua (1:50).
Cover tubes with aluminum foil and incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Without washing, add 20 μL of Fc blocking buffer (1:10).
Incubate at room temperature for another 10 min.
Add 20 μL of each antibody to the sample tube as required.
Vortex briefly to mix thoroughly.
Cover tubes completely with aluminum foil.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 minutes in the dark.
Wash with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Vortex briefly after washing.
Centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet with approximately 120 μL of FACS buffer.
Combine spleen cells with ovarian cells for single-stained and fluorescence minus one (FMO) controls in an approximate ratio of 3:1 to 0.5, respectively.
Use approximately 2–5 million cells per fully stained ovary and spleen sample, respectively.
Include ovarian cells in the FMO controls to ensure accurate gating.
Data collection timing is estimated at 3-4 hours depending on sample size.
Collect data on the flow cytometer.
Use unstained samples, stained compensation beads, and single-stained samples to set appropriate PMT voltages.
Place all events in the linear range of each detector.
Calculate compensation.
Exclude non-cellular debris using a FSC-A by SSC-A light scatter gate during analysis.
Exclude doublets and aggregated cells using a FSC-A by FSC-H gate.
Select Zombie Aqua negative live cells for subsequent analysis.
Identify T cells as CD45+CD3+ cells.
Classify further as CD8+ and CD4+ T cells.
Gate double negative T (DNT) cells by excluding CD8+, CD4+, and NK1.1+ cells.
Identify NKT cells as CD3+ CD4-, CD8-, and NK1.1+.
